children.name: Mesitornis
children.description: Medium-sized, terrestrial birds endemic to Madagascar with a slender, slightly curved bill and a long, graduated tail. They are elusive, secretive inhabitants of the forest floor, more often heard than seen.

children.name: Mesitornis variegatus
children.description: The white-breasted mesite or white-breasted roatelo (Mesitornis variegatus) is a ground-dwelling bird endemic to Madagascar. One of three species in the mesite family, Mesitornithidae, it is classified as vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). It has a small population and is restricted to five sites in the north and west of the island, and one in the east.

children.name: Mesitornis unicolor
children.description: The brown mesite (Mesitornis unicolor) is a ground-dwelling bird endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Monias
children.description: A monotypic genus restricted to the arid spiny forests of southern Madagascar, showing pronounced sexual dimorphism unlike the other mesite genus. It has a longer, more decurved bill adapted for probing in dry soil.

children.name: Monias benschi
children.description: The subdesert mesite (Monias benschi) is a ground-dwelling bird endemic to Madagascar.
